name: Notesnook
insteadOf: Evernote / Notion / Microsoft OneNote / Google Keep
hook: A fully open-source, zero-knowledge end-to-end encrypted note-taking app with markdown support and cross-platform sync.
bullets: True zero-knowledge architecture: notes, tags, and attachments are client-side encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305
Rich-text and markdown editor with math equations, checklists, tables, and code blocks
Cross-platform sync across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, and modern web browsers
Private password-protected vaults, biometric app locking, and clean offline-first storage
benefits: Never worry about note providers, hackers, or server administrators snooping on your personal thoughts
Seamlessly write on desktop and look up your notes on mobile with instant sync
No vendor lock-in: export your entire notebook anytime to standard Markdown, HTML, or PDF
100% open-source client and server code independently audited for cryptographic security
setupSteps: Download Notesnook for your platform (desktop, mobile, or use the web app)
Create a free account and safely back up your cryptographic recovery key
Create notebooks, organize with tags, and start writing in rich text or Markdown
Lock sensitive notebooks in individual vaults for biometric or PIN protection
details: Notesnook is a private, encrypted note-taking application designed as a zero-knowledge alternative to Evernote and Notion. Every note, notebook title, tag, attachment, and revision is encrypted on your device using XChaCha20-Poly1305 and Argon2id before syncing, ensuring that not even the Notesnook servers can view your content. The app provides a powerful editing experience supporting Markdown, LaTeX math equations, code blocks with syntax highlighting, nested notebooks, reminders, and dark/light themes. Notesnook works entirely offline and syncs smoothly across mobile and desktop. It is 100% open source under the GPL-3.0 license and has undergone public independent security audits.
setup: App (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, Web) — installer or app stores
